items.title: Dive into Deep Learning
items.authors: Aston Zhang, Zachary C. Lipton, Mu Li & Alexander J. Smola
items.description: Build intuition and working models together. Follow executable examples from linear regression through attention, transformers, computer vision, and modern neural architectures.

items.title: Understanding Deep Learning
items.authors: Simon J. D. Prince
items.description: Explore neural networks through careful diagrams, experiments, and mathematics. Connect training fundamentals with transformers, diffusion, graph networks, and the questions behind generalization.

items.title: The Little Book of Deep Learning
items.authors: François Fleuret
items.description: A compact, phone-friendly tour for readers with a STEM background. Connect training, architectures, generative models, and efficient adaptation in a few focused sittings.

items.title: Neural Networks and Deep Learning
items.authors: Michael Nielsen
items.description: Start with handwritten digits and discover how a network learns. Interactive explanations make gradients, backpropagation, and the role of hidden layers feel tangible.

items.title: Deep Learning
items.authors: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio & Aaron Courville
items.description: A foundational reference connecting probability, optimization, representation learning, and deep generative models. Read the complete authorized web edition, with a chapter for every detour.

items.title: Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts
items.authors: Christopher M. Bishop & Hugh Bishop
items.description: Follow a visual, probability-based path from basic learning principles to modern deep architectures. The authors provide a free browser reader alongside the print edition.

items.title: Deep Learning for Coders
items.authors: Jeremy Howard & Sylvain Gugger
items.description: Learn by building useful models first, then unpacking their internals. The authors share the book as readable, runnable notebooks covering vision, text, and tabular data.

items.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
items.authors: Marc Peter Deisenroth, A. Aldo Faisal & Cheng Soon Ong
items.description: Grow the mathematical roots behind ML: vectors, calculus, probability, and optimization. Then see those ideas become regression, PCA, mixture models, and support vector machines.

items.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Python
items.authors: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani & Jonathan Taylor
items.description: A welcoming route through regression, classification, resampling, trees, and deep learning. Python labs turn statistical ideas into experiments you can reproduce and extend.

items.title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
items.authors: Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani & Jerome Friedman
items.description: Go deeper into statistical prediction, regularization, kernels, ensembles, and unsupervised learning. This authorized second-edition PDF includes corrections from the twelfth printing.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
items.authors: Kevin P. Murphy
items.description: View prediction through uncertainty. This author-shared draft connects probability, decision theory, classical algorithms, and neural models, with notebooks that recreate many of its figures.

items.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: Advanced Topics
items.authors: Kevin P. Murphy
items.description: Explore inference, latent variables, generative modeling, and sequential decisions. The freely shared author draft links theory to practical notebook experiments and modern deep learning.

items.title: Speech and Language Processing
items.authors: Dan Jurafsky & James H. Martin
items.description: Trace language systems from tokens and embeddings to transformers, post-training, and retrieval. This evolving third-edition draft also covers speech and linguistic structure.

items.title: Graph Representation Learning
items.authors: William L. Hamilton
items.description: Learn to represent relationships, not just individual examples. This authorized author draft explores node embeddings, graph neural networks, knowledge graphs, and graph generation.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
items.authors: Richard S. Sutton & Andrew G. Barto
items.description: Follow an agent learning through rewards, exploration, and experience. The second edition develops bandits, value functions, temporal-difference learning, and policy gradients from first principles.

items.title: Introduction to Machine Learning Systems
items.authors: Vijay Janapa Reddi & contributors
items.description: Connect models to the machines that run them. Volume I covers data workflows, training, compression, acceleration, serving, and the trade-offs behind reliable ML systems.

items.title: Machine Learning Systems at Scale
items.authors: Vijay Janapa Reddi & contributors
items.description: Take ML beyond one machine. This open Volume II draft explores distributed training, communication, inference fleets, fault tolerance, and responsible operation at scale.

items.title: The Principles of Deep Learning Theory
items.authors: Daniel A. Roberts, Sho Yaida & Boris Hanin
items.description: An ambitious mathematical exploration of why deep networks behave as they do. The author preprint studies initialization, learning dynamics, representation, and finite-width effects.

items.title: Essence of Linear Algebra
items.description: See vectors, matrices, transformations, and eigenvectors as geometry. Build the visual intuition that makes embeddings, optimization, and neural networks easier to understand.

items.title: Seeing Theory
items.description: Play with probability, distributions, Bayesian inference, and regression through an archived collection of interactive visualizations. Turn abstract statistical ideas into experiments you can see.

items.title: Neural Networks, Visually
items.description: Follow the geometry of neurons, gradient descent, and backpropagation before exploring transformers and attention. Animated explanations make the mathematics feel connected and approachable.

items.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
items.description: Build a practical foundation in regression, classification, data preparation, embeddings, and model evaluation through short lessons, interactive diagrams, and hands-on programming exercises.

items.title: CS229: Machine Learning
items.description: Study the mathematical foundations of supervised learning, clustering, and reinforcement learning with archived lectures and assignments. A rigorous companion to practical model building.

items.title: CS50: AI with Python
items.description: Build Python projects around search, uncertainty, optimization, learning, and language. The OpenCourseWare lessons are free; optional verified certificates and academic credit are separate.

items.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
items.description: Start by building useful models, then unpack how they work. Explore vision, language, tabular data, and deployment with practical notebooks and a freely readable companion book.

items.title: 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
items.description: Explore neural network foundations and modern applications with MIT lecture recordings, slides, and programming labs. Practice the ideas through the openly published course materials.

items.title: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
items.description: Go deeper into visual recognition, convolutional networks, training, and modern vision architectures. Use public course notes, slides, assignments, and linked lecture recordings for independent study.

items.title: PyTorch: Learn the Basics
items.description: Build a complete image classification workflow while learning tensors, datasets, automatic differentiation, optimization, and model saving. Run the examples locally or in linked notebooks.

items.title: The LLM Course
items.description: Move from tokenizers and transformers to datasets, fine-tuning, and reasoning models. Learn through open lessons and notebooks using the Hugging Face ecosystem.

items.title: AI Agents Course
items.description: Understand tools, actions, observations, and agent workflows. Build with agent libraries, work through practical use cases, and explore evaluation with openly available course lessons.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Course
items.description: Train agents that learn from rewards and interaction. Connect reinforcement learning theory to hands-on environments, practical notebooks, and community challenges in an open course.

items.title: CS224N: NLP with Deep Learning
items.description: Study word vectors, language models, and neural approaches to language. Follow public notes, assignments, and free lecture archives; enrolled classroom services are separate.

items.title: Neural Network Playground
items.description: Change layers, features, learning rate, and regularization while a small network trains in your browser. Watch decision boundaries and loss respond to each experiment.

items.title: CNN Explainer
items.description: Follow an image through a convolutional network and inspect its intermediate operations. Connect filters, activations, and pooling to the predictions a network eventually makes.

items.title: Transformer Explainer
items.description: Trace GPT-2 text generation through token embeddings, attention, and output probabilities. Adjust sampling controls and inspect how a transformer chooses its next token.

items.title: Feature Visualization
items.description: Explore how optimization can reveal patterns that activate a network. Rich visual examples connect neurons, features, and interpretability while explaining the method's limitations.

items.title: The Illustrated Transformer
items.description: Build an intuitive picture of the original transformer architecture through diagrams of encoders, decoders, queries, keys, values, and multi-head attention, one step at a time.

items.title: Full Stack Deep Learning
items.description: Take a model beyond a notebook. The free 2022 course covers data, experiments, testing, deployment, monitoring, and the engineering decisions behind practical ML products.

items.title: Made With ML
items.description: Connect ML development with software engineering through open lessons and code covering data, training, evaluation, serving, testing, and CI/CD. Compute and hosted services are separate.

items.title: People + AI Guidebook
items.description: Design AI products around people with patterns, case studies, and worksheets. Explore user needs, calibrated trust, meaningful explanations, feedback, control, and graceful recovery from errors.

items.title: Recommendation Systems
items.description: Learn how recommenders retrieve and rank useful items. Connect collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, and deep models to the choices behind personalized recommendations.

items.title: Palantir AIP: From Data to Actions
items.description: Explore public documentation for ontology-connected AI workflows, Logic, evaluation, and assistants. Reading is free; using the platform requires a suitable Palantir enrollment.
